body.statement: For every rational interior one-mechanism affine family, the following are equivalent: \(\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}\) with \(E_Tq=0\) and \(b_Tq\neq0\); and \(\operatorname{rank}([E_T;b_T])>\operatorname{rank}(E_T)\). The condition is independent of the rational basis \(R_T\). Whenever it holds, rational row reduction yields \(v=R_Tq\), and there is a computable \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) such that every \(t\in\mathbb Q\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\) keeps \(\theta+t v\) normalized and strictly positive, preserves the entire normalized selected observational law and \(D_{\rho}\) exactly, and changes \(N_{\rho}\). Thus \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) returns a positive rational pair certifying nonidentification of \(\psi\) in \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations, and \(\operatorname{Verify}\) checks the expanded certificate in \(\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.
body.justification: The theorem turns a numerical or symbolic fiber direction into an exact, portable, positive rational causal nonidentification certificate.
body.gap: Discrete polynomial programs describe observational fibers, but the checked literature does not isolate an exact simplex-tangent criterion that simultaneously locks a selected conditional denominator and separates its numerator.
body.consumer: A graph search or algebraic solver can hand one passing template to the compiler and obtain a certificate that a third party verifies without trusting the search.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a family satisfying Definitions \texttt{def:affine-mechanism-family} and \texttt{def:affine-rank-system}.  In particular, \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)\), the represented coordinates \(\mathcal M,\mathcal G,F,F'\) and \(R_F\) are fixed, and exactly one normalized local table is changed from \(\theta\) to \(\theta+t v\), where \(v=R_Tq\in T\).  All state spaces used by this certificate are finite and binary by Definition \texttt{def:rational-binary-class}; the target model class itself remains the published positive discrete class.

We first establish exact affinity.  Fix either the observational regime or the terminal regime \(\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x)\), and fix a complete assignment \(\omega\) of the nonintervened endogenous and latent variables.  In the truncated SCM factorization, the varied local table contributes either one coordinate \(\theta_{j(\omega)}+t v_{j(\omega)}\), or no coordinate if its endogenous variable is intervened upon.  Every other factor is fixed.  Consequently the complete-assignment mass has one of the two forms
\[
 p_t(\omega)
 =\bigl(\theta_{j(\omega)}+t v_{j(\omega)}\bigr)
   \prod_{\ell\ne j(\omega)}p_\ell(\omega)
 =p_0(\omega)+t\dot p(\omega)
\]
or \(p_t(\omega)=p_0(\omega)\).  Marginalization is a finite sum, so there are rational directional coefficients, linear in \(v\), such that
\[
\begin{aligned}
 o_z(t)&=o_z(0)+t\dot o_z(v),&
 Z_o(t)&=Z_o(0)+t\dot Z_o(v),\\
 h(t)&=h(0)+t\dot h(v),&
 k(t)&=k(0)+t\dot k(v),&
 Z_x(t)&=Z_x(0)+t\dot Z_x(v).
\end{aligned}                                                    \tag{1}
\]
This proves, rather than assumes, the affine property used below.  Strict positivity of the base mechanisms implies
\[
 Z_o(0)>0,\qquad Z_x(0)>0,\qquad h(0)>0.             \tag{2}
\]
Indeed, each is a finite sum containing positive complete-assignment masses, and the event defining \(h(0)\) is a supported assignment of the positive discrete model.

For every \(t\) for which the perturbed model remains positive, cross-multiplication in (1) gives, cell by cell,
\[
 \frac{o_z(t)}{Z_o(t)}-\frac{o_z(0)}{Z_o(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_o(0)\dot o_z(v)-o_z(0)\dot Z_o(v)\}}
        {Z_o(t)Z_o(0)},                               \tag{3}
\]
and similarly
\[
\begin{aligned}
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-D_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 &=\frac{h(t)}{Z_x(t)}-\frac{h(0)}{Z_x(0)}\\
 &=\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot h(v)-h(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)},                               \tag{4}\\
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-N_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 &=\frac{k(t)}{Z_x(t)}-\frac{k(0)}{Z_x(0)}\\
 &=\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot k(v)-k(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)}.                               \tag{5}
\end{aligned}
\]
The possible products of two slopes cancel in each difference, so (3)--(5) are exact identities, not first-order approximations.  By Definition \texttt{def:affine-rank-system}, after writing \(v=R_Tq\), all braces in (3), followed by the brace in (4), form \(E_Tq\), whereas the brace in (5) is \(b_Tq\).

We next prove the rank criterion over \(\mathbb Q\).  If \(b_T\) is in the row space of \(E_T\), then \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  Conversely, suppose \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  The formula
\[
 \ell(E_Tq)=b_Tq                                             \tag{6}
\]
defines a rational linear functional on \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\), because two preimages of the same vector differ by an element of \(\ker(E_T)\).  Extend a rational basis of \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\) to a basis of its ambient rational vector space and extend \(\ell\) arbitrarily on the added basis vectors.  Then (6) says that \(b_T=\ell E_T\), so \(b_T\) is in the row space of \(E_T\).  Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}:\ E_Tq=0\ \text{ and }\ b_Tq\ne0\\
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow b_T\notin\operatorname{row}(E_T)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}E_T\\ b_T\end{bmatrix}
 >\operatorname{rank}(E_T).                              \tag{7}
\end{aligned}
\]
Rational row reduction decides (7) and, in the strict-rank case, returns a rational null vector \(q\) with \(b_Tq\ne0\).

The criterion does not depend on the chosen rational basis of \(T\).  If \(R_T'\) is another basis matrix, then \(R_T'=R_TH\) for an invertible rational matrix \(H\).  Hence
\[
 ER_T'=E_TH,\qquad bR_T'=b_TH.                            \tag{8}
\]
Right multiplication by \(H\) preserves both ranks in (7), and the coordinate change \(q'=H^{-1}q\) preserves the mechanism direction \(R_T'q'=R_Tq\).  This proves basis independence.

It remains to choose an interval that preserves both positivity and membership in the represented model class.  For the returned \(q\), put \(v=R_Tq\).  Since \(b_Tq=bv\ne0\), one has \(v\ne0\).  Define the positive rational simplex radius
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{pos}}
 =\frac12\min_{j:v_j\ne0}
 \left\{\frac{\theta_j}{|v_j|},
             \frac{1-\theta_j}{|v_j|}\right\}.          \tag{9}
\]
Because \(v\in T\), its coordinates sum to zero in every probability block.  Thus \(\theta+t v\) is normalized, and (9) implies \(0<\theta_j+t v_j<1\) for every coordinate whenever \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{pos}}\).

Positivity alone is not used to infer graph representation.  The parent domains, structural incidence, latent incidence, selection vertices, and all unvaried mechanisms are fixed by Definition \texttt{def:affine-mechanism-family}.  No forbidden parent can be introduced because the varied table has the same indexing parent set.  If membership in the represented realization treats parent sets as nonminimal compatibility sets, these facts already preserve \(\mathcal G\).  If the representation convention requires every displayed parent to remain active, let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite set of displayed parent incidences whose activity is witnessed in the varied table.  Since \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\) realizes \(\mathcal G\), for each \(a\in\mathcal A\) choose two entries, differing only in the value of that parent while the other arguments and the child value are fixed, for which
\[
 \alpha_a=\theta_{j_a}-\theta_{j_a'}\ne0.
\]
Put \(\beta_a=v_{j_a}-v_{j_a'}\) and define
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{act}}
 =\begin{cases}
  1,&\text{if }\beta_a=0\text{ for every }a\in\mathcal A,\\
  \displaystyle\min\!\left\{1,
       \frac12\min_{a:\beta_a\ne0}\frac{|\alpha_a|}{|\beta_a|}\right\},
       &\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}                                               \tag{10}
\]
For \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{act}}\),
\[
 |\alpha_a+t\beta_a|
 \ge |\alpha_a|-|t|\,|\beta_a|>\frac12|\alpha_a|>0        \tag{11}
\]
whenever \(\beta_a\ne0\), while the contrast is unchanged when \(\beta_a=0\).  Thus every required active parent stays active.  Equations (10)--(11), together with the unchanged structural and latent incidence, show directly that the perturbed SCM has the same represented graph \(\mathcal G\), hence remains represented by \(\mathcal M\in[\mathcal P]_{\mathsf M}\).  Set
\[
 \delta=\min\{\delta_{\mathrm{pos}},\delta_{\mathrm{act}}\}. \tag{12}
\]
All quantities in (9)--(12) are rational and computable from the supplied tables.  For every rational \(t\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\), the perturbed mechanisms are rational, normalized, strictly positive, binary, and compatible with the same represented realization.  Therefore, by Definition \texttt{def:rational-binary-class},
\[
 \mathbf M(0),\mathbf M(t)
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P).                    \tag{13}
\]

Assume now that the equivalent conditions in (7) hold and take any rational \(t\) in the interval (12).  Let \(\mathbf M_0=\mathbf M(0)\) and \(\mathbf M_1=\mathbf M(t)\).  Since all normalizers in (3)--(5) are positive, \(E_Tq=0\) and (3)--(4) yield
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_0}
 =P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_1},
 \qquad
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}=D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}>0.            \tag{14}
\]
The equality of the observational laws in (14) holds for every full observed cell \(z\), hence for the entire normalized selected observational law.  On the other hand, \(b_Tq\ne0\), \(t\ne0\), and (5) give
\[
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}\ne N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}.           \tag{15}
\]
By Definitions \texttt{def:target-query} and \texttt{def:locked-certificate}, the normalized terminal conditional is
\[
 Q_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y;\bar x,\bar c)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x),
                         \bar C=\bar c,S=\mathbf1)
 =\frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
        {D_{\rho,\mathbf M}(\bar c;\bar x)}.              \tag{16}
\]
Thus (14)--(16) make the two terminal conditionals unequal.

The legal trace contained in the locked certificate starts at \(\rho_0=(X,C)\) and ends at \(\rho\), by Definition \texttt{def:reachable-role-graph}.  At each edge, the moved nonempty role intersection satisfies the stated Chen--Mooij Rule--2 separation.  Apply \texttt{lem:selected-rule-two} with its outcome set equal to \(Y\), its exchange set equal to that moved intersection, and its remaining action and conditioning sets equal to the current role sets.  Its positivity premise holds by (13).  The two adjacent conditional kernels are therefore equal.  Induction over the finite trace gives, for \(j\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
 Q_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}(y;\bar x,\bar c)
 =Q_{\rho_0,\mathbf M_j}(y;x,c)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M_j}(y;x,c).                              \tag{17}
\]
Equations (15)--(17) imply \(\psi_{\mathbf M_0}\ne\psi_{\mathbf M_1}\), whereas (14) gives equality of their full selected observational laws.  Since the pair lies in the rational binary subclass in (13), it is also a pair in the published class quantified over by Definition \texttt{def:identification}; the negative conclusion therefore transfers upward to that class.  No positive completeness transfer from the binary subclass is being asserted.  The supplied represented graph, forest, and trace satisfy the remaining clauses of Definition \texttt{def:locked-certificate}, so \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) returns the claimed \(\Gamma\).

Finally, we prove the complexity bounds in the stated expanded encodings.  Clear denominators in \(E_T\) and \(b_T\), and use fraction-free Gaussian elimination.  If the integerized matrix has dimensions bounded by \(s\) and input entries of bit length at most \(B\), every elimination value is a minor of an input submatrix.  The Leibniz formula bounds the absolute value of an \(r\)-by-\(r\) minor by \(r!2^{rB}\), so its bit length is at most
\[
 rB+\log_2(r!)+1=O\bigl(s(B+\log s)\bigr).              \tag{18}
\]
There are polynomially many arithmetic operations, and (18) bounds their bit sizes polynomially.  The rank test, a rational null vector, the active-parent witnesses, (9)--(12), and a choice such as \(t=\delta/2\) are consequently computable in polynomial time in \(L_{\mathrm{temp}}\).

The compiler then copies the supplied graph, trace, and forest data and enumerates the dense complete-assignment tables.  Each displayed atom is obtained by a product of encoded local probabilities and each displayed marginal by a sum over entries that are themselves part of the expanded output.  Sequential exact products and sums have bit length polynomial in the total input-plus-output bit length.  Hence compilation, including writing \(\Gamma\), takes \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations.

For verification, acyclicity, ancestry, latent projection, endpoint compatibility, role-edge legality, and the forest predicates are finite incidence or reachability checks.  If a representation convention is verified through its full separation model, an exhaustive check is still polynomial in the expanded certificate length: the dense observed table already has at least \(2^n\) entries, while the collection of disjoint vertex triples has at most \(4^n\) members.  The verifier checks every probability block for exact normalization and strict positivity, checks the active-parent witnesses from (11), recomputes the displayed observational and interventional atoms from the dense rational factorization, and verifies (14)--(15) by exact cross-multiplication.  The number and bit length of all inputs to these operations are bounded by \(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma}\).  Therefore \(\operatorname{Verify}\) runs in \(\operatorname{poly}(|\mathcal P|+L_{\Gamma})\) bit operations, completing the proof.
